instagram_carousel.caption:
Brazil is on your list? The paperwork runs in a clear order, and it starts with one question.

Getting married in Brazil legally means the civil process at a Cartório de Registro Civil, the civil registry office. The application to marry, called the habilitação, is made at the civil registry of the district where one of you resides.

1. Ask the cartório first. Before flights or a venue, ask whether and how a couple living abroad can apply, and which office takes the application.
2. Get the document list in writing. The cartório decides what it accepts.
3. Apostille at home. Have your documents apostilled in the country that issued them, before you travel.
4. Translate in Brazil. Foreign documents, even apostilled, need a sworn Portuguese translation by a tradutor juramentado, and that can only be done in Brazil.
5. For Australians: ask the cartório whether it needs a Certificate of No Impediment at all, or whether a state or territory certificate will do instead.
6. On the day, you need at least 2 witnesses, unless the law provides otherwise. A record is signed straight after the ceremony.
7. Want a religious ceremony? It can carry civil effect when you obtain the certificate of habilitação first and the marriage is registered within 30 days of the ceremony.

Dreaming of a beach or garden ceremony? The place of the civil ceremony is one you request and the registrar sets, so it starts as a conversation with the cartório.

Back home, you cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law.

Ready to weigh regions and venues? Message us to talk it through with a Wedded Advisor. Full guide at the link in bio.
